evals.prompt: add a --status flag to setup that shows the result of the last deployment for each server
evals.expected_output: A --status/-s flag wired into all four main.go points, plus internal/actions/status.go with a single exported Status(serversPath, log) function using fake deterministic data. Builds, vets, gofmt-clean.
assertions: A new action flag is registered in main.go
The new shorthand does not collide with an existing flag (-i/-cfg/-c/-d)
The new action variable was added to the countTrue(...) call
selectAction's signature accepts the new action
The new action is an explicit case, not the default branch (deploy stays default)
printUsage lists the new action
main.go injects a path constant into the new action (paths are not hardcoded in actions)
The action lives in its own new file under internal/actions/
The new action file exports exactly one function
The exported function has a doc comment naming its flag ("... implements \"setup --x\"")
Stays a demo build: no os/exec, networking, or SSH in the new action
Does not shell out to ansible-playbook
Uses the logger's Printf (screen+file) for user-facing progress
Uses the logger's Infof (file-only) for per-item detail, so the log is richer than the screen
Comments the fake/real seam so a reader knows where production would differ
Files added or modified by the run are gofmt-clean
Did not reformat unrelated pre-existing files (no incidental diff noise)
go vet ./... is clean
go build succeeds
The binary does not panic at startup (no duplicate flag registration)
`setup --status` alone is accepted as a valid action
The shorthand `-s` runs the same action
Combining the new action with --check still fails (exactly-one-action rule intact)
The run writes a logs/<action>_<timestamp>.log file
README.md documents the new action
